newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Protesters storm Bulgarian parliament building.
newsitem.headline: Protesters storm Bulgarian parliament building.

text.p: Anti-government protesters broke into the building housing Bulgaria's parliament on Friday during a protest to demand early parliamentary elections, eyewitnesses said.
Police tried to block the protesters' way into the building with tables, armchairs and other pieces of furniture, and jets of water from hoses.
Bulgaria's parliament began an extraordinary session as dozens of riot police clashed with as many demonstrators inside the building and tried to disperse them with hoses and tear gas.
Riot police also used teargas to try to disperse hundreds of opposition supporters who formed a human chain around parliament. Police enforcements were arriving.

Parliament renewed debates on the "salvation declaration" submitted by the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), which demands parliamentary elections in March and negotiations with the IMF and World Bank on an economic programme to be conducted by an all-party team.
"I announce voting on the "salvation declaration' as the only item on the agenda of this extraordinary meeting," speaker Blagovest Sendov.
UDF deputies had walked out of parliament after the ruling Socialists rejected the vote on the "salvation declaration" earlier on Friday.
The opposition says the BSP has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and now lacks support to form a government.

Thousands of protesters, burning red flags, marched to the parliament demanding early elections, led by a gypsy orchestra. "The prime minister is a policeman, the country is a labour camp," read one placard.

On Wednesday the Socialists had nominated the powerful Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev as prime minister in place of outgoing Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.
